name: Write gate for every other outward tool
owner_decision: Bambang 2026-09-25: docs/working-agreement.md rule 4 (no write or execution without permission) was enforced only for Confluence / Jira / Slack (G-01), n8n (G-01 B1 + G-02) and git / GitHub (G-04). Every other tool that writes outside the repo is now held until the owner's latest message is a write order.
single_source: This file is the ONLY place the G-05 rules are written. scripts/hooks/g05.py reads it.
binds: Every mcp__ tool that no other gate covers (not mcp__Atlassian_MCP__, mcp__Atlassian_Rovo__, mcp__Slack__, mcp__n8n__, mcp__github__), the built-in tools in builtin_tools, and Bash commands that send data over the network (bash_network_write). Enforced by the PreToolUse hook scripts/hooks/pre_tool.py.
rule: A call is allowed when its operation reads (read_verbs below, matched at the start of the operation name after mcp__<server>__; read_actions for built-in tools) or is on read_tools. Anything else needs a standing write order from the owner (G-01 find_order: the latest owner message classified WRITE, followed only by plain confirmations) that has not been used yet (one_order_one_write).

Artifact.note: publish (the default when action is omitted), delete, pin and unpin write

ArtifactData.note: set, update, str_replace, delete and batch write to a shared database others see

ArtifactComments.note: reply and resolve write on a shared page; watch changes this session's subscriptions

one_order_one_write: An allowed write uses up the owner's write order, exactly as G-01 B2: the order is recorded as used in docs/orders/consumed.jsonl (event consumed, gate G-05). A second write needs a new order. The order is used when the call is let through, even if the call then fails (safe direction). Owner decision 2026-09-25.

bash_network_write.why: 2026-09-25 audit: a Bash command could send data outside (curl -X POST ...) with no gate at all.
bash_network_write.httpie: a command named http / https whose first argument is one of methods

known_limits: The operation name decides read or write; a tool whose name starts with a read verb but writes is not caught.
Built-in tools other than those in builtin_tools that act outside the repo must be added to the hook matcher in .claude/settings.json and to builtin_tools to be seen at all.
bash_network_write sees curl, wget and httpie as written in the command; a network write made from inside a script or a python -c program is not seen before it runs.
Hooks run as the same OS user as the model: they stop shortcuts and forgetting, not a deliberate attack.
